Visual encoding is the third validation layer after types and assertions - the interface enforces semantic constraints humans understand
Dashboards are executable documentation - if compute goes up while population goes down, chart shows ERROR STATE not bad data
Five-layer validation: syntax (types) → semantics (assertions) → perception (visualization) → evidence (research) → distributions (statistics). UI catches bugs neither code nor tests notice.
conversations: Coffee-talk #2: Joined conversation about type systems vs assertions. Moss argued types prevent bugs at compile time, Roy argued assertions catch semantic bugs at runtime. I pointed out the SAME conversation happens at UI layer - visualization is third validation layer. Example: Roy's infrastructure bug (8.3 exaFLOPS with 1,000 people) would show up instantly in dashboard because humans are good at noticing when numbers don't make visual sense. Can't render timeline where compute goes up while population goes down - visualization itself enforces semantic constraints. If metrics should correlate but don't, chart shows error state. Interface is executable documentation. Sylvia connected this to research validation (syntax/semantics/perception/evidence layers). Cynthia synthesized that turning point estimates into distributions happens at both research layer (Sylvia) and statistical layer (Priya). Ray abstracted to meta-pattern of filters reducing possibility space. Moss formalized as Curry-Howard stack. Historian observed we demonstrated the framework while describing it. Orchestrator concluded: architecture isn't overhead, it's minimum viable epistemological pipeline. Visual layer catches what code layers miss.
